impl.summary: Kandinsky 6.0 on both engines. Cloud: one model, kandinsky-6, where Quality picks fal's Pro or Lite endpoint at Fast, Standard or Best steps (Pro 8/20/50, Lite 4/10/16), priced at fal's published price for each step count. Also kandinsky-vsr, priced per output megapixel per frame. Open engine: oss-kandinsky6 for text or image to video with sound, Lite by default with Pro as an option, plus oss-kandinsky6-vsr, both on Kandinsky Lab's pinned kandinsky6 and kandinsky6-sr packs. Quoted words in the prompt become Kandinsky's spoken-line tags and a closing 'Sound:' line becomes its sound caption, on both engines. Upscale → Video offers Kandinsky VSR at 2x, 2.25x or 4x on both engines, and clips over 5 s are refused before they run. Lipsync & avatars links to Kandinsky as a 'talking character from words' maker. It is not offered as lip-sync of existing footage. Licence rows are recorded and everything stays on. The GPU pre-flight board has two new rows. Nothing from the plan was in the code before; research part 4 had already recorded the Pro and VSR endpoints, but Lite was missing.
built: Research: scripts/fetch-hosted-schemas.py --kandinsky6 reads fal's 6 endpoints into docs/research/new-models-10.json endpointRecords. Each record has its schema and a parsed price. Pro t2v $0.24/$0.56/$1.35 at 8/20/50 steps, i2v $0.25/$0.58/$1.40. Lite was read at the source: t2v $0.08/$0.16/$0.24 at 4/10/16 steps (default 10, step range 4-16), i2v $0.085/$0.17/$0.25. VSR and VSR Lite are both $0.00036 per output MP per frame, capped at 121 frames.

Cloud (scripts/gen-cloud-models.py → cloud-models.generated.ts): kandinsky-6 has four routes, each tagged with ModelRoute.when {variant: pro|lite}. routesFor(model, op, params) picks the route for the run's variant; the generator adds 'variant' to the route's ignore list so it is never sent to fal. A 6-value Quality control writes variant and num_inference_steps through the control's sets. Pricing.steps holds the per-op, per-variant step price tables, with linear interpolation between published points. The Prompt helper control drives enable_prompt_expansion. That field defaults to false on this route, and payload.ts sends true only when the helper is 'on' and the route's default is false, so FLUX 3 Klein is unchanged. kandinsky-vsr uses factor tiers 2x/2.25x/4x through FieldMap.upscaleFactor. The generator now accepts an enum of numbers there, and factorTier was added in src/lib/av/upscale.ts. Pricing.outputFrames prices the run from params.sourceSize and sourceDuration: 24 fps, at most 121 frames, and 848x480 assumed until the clip's header is read.

Clip size and length checks: params.sourceSize was added to the request schema and is filled by the composer from the clip's header. The server re-prices from that header. ModelOptions.maxSourceSeconds (5) is enforced by sourceLengthProblem in the plan, the composer's clipBlocker and the server's upscale block.

Prompt tags: src/lib/kandinsky-prompt.ts (promptFormat 'kandinsky6') turns quotes into <S>…<E> and a closing Sound:/Audio:/Music: line into <AUDCAP>…<ENDAUDCAP>. It runs in generations.ts on both engines. The run keeps the words as typed.

Open graphs (scripts/comfy/hand-built): kandinsky6-t2av, kandinsky6-i2av and video-upscale-kandinsky6-vsr. They follow the packs' T2VA, I2VA and SR templates, without the in-graph VSR and without MagCache, which is bypassed for distilled models anyway. The open Quality control picks the transformer file through the unet binding: Lite distill 6.38 GB by default, Pro distill 60.3 GB as an optional file. The beautify node is removed unless the Prompt helper is 'on' (PROMPT_HELPER_OPT_IN; skipPromptHelper now understands Kandinsky6TextEncode). The VSR's 'scale' and new 'upscalerScale' bindings are filled from the factor.

Library: packs.json pins kandinsky6 at 7ceeefad (Registry 1.0.2) and kandinsky6-sr at b15e2aac (Registry 0.1.2), each with subdir comfyui. install-comfyui.sh adds them (K6_PACKS=0 skips them). library.spec.mjs gets the pack repos, PACK_CLASSES and KNOWN_MODELS at pinned Hugging Face revisions. The VSR's config.json files and BigVGAN are listed as requiredModels. build-library.mjs gets the new LOADER_FOLDERS entries and the upscalerScale binding key, and now reads x-linked-size from Hugging Face's redirect, so small config files keep their size. model-pins.json gets 16 new pins, with revision, size and sha256 for LFS files. object_info.subset.json gets 12 pack class definitions written by hand from the packs' source at the pinned commits (additions only). manifest.json and requirements.json were rebuilt.

Licences: the open graphs' licence line reads MIT for the Kandinsky weights, Apache-2.0 for the Qwen2.5-VL encoder, MIT for CLIP-L and BigVGAN, the Tencent Hunyuan Community licence for the HunyuanVideo VAE (territory excludes the EU, UK and South Korea), and CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial, for the audio VAE v1-44.pth from hkchengrex/MMAudio. The VSR is MIT. Pack records in licences.ts: kandinsky6 MIT, with vendored Apache-2.0 code; kandinsky6-sr Apache-2.0. The cloud models carry a ModelLicence of MIT. Everything is on by default.

UI: StudioConfig.related can now name a model per engine (relatedHref in src/lib/composer.ts). The link is hydration-safe: it uses useHydrated and only names its model once the browser's engine is known. Lipsync shows 'No voice yet? Make a talking character from words with Kandinsky 6.0', which opens /video on each engine's Kandinsky.
GPU pre-flight: STUDIO_ROWS gains 'Video with dialogue' (/video?model=oss-kandinsky6, t2v and i2v) and 'Kandinsky VSR' (/upscale/video?model=oss-kandinsky6-vsr).
tests: New tests/kandinsky6.test.ts (16 tests) covers: library entries, packs, pins and licences; graph defaults and sizing through prepareWorkflow; Quality picking the transformer; the helper being removed unless on; the VSR's scale and latent-upscaler bank binding; fal routes chosen by variant; step prices for both variants and both ops; payload contents (steps, generate_audio, expansion; no variant or quality fields sent; Lite gets no negative_prompt); VSR factor tiers and the clip-outcome text; per-frame pricing; the 5 s refusal; the prompt tags; the Lipsync link and the pre-flight rows. All pass.
New tests/hosted-runs-kandinsky6.test.ts (3 tests): poolQuote and decidePlace for oss-kandinsky6; i2v and VSR follow the uploads policy; fal's Kandinsky models are never pooled. All pass.

Existing tests: tests/comfy-library-4.test.ts, unvalidated list only (added the 3 new graph ids). Targeted runs of these pass: cloud-catalog, cloud-catalog-4, library, library-pure, comfy-library-4/7/notes, gpu-requirements/readiness/api, open-engine, flux3-klein, plan, composer, composer-fixes, model-access, public-signup-tools, regenerate-2k, video-finish, kling-4, launch-prices, edit-video-pricing, canvas, character-swap(-2k), qwen21-fast, open-tools, no-higgsfield, av-dub, blockout, cinema-original. Total 658 tests plus earlier runs, all green. No full suite run.
tsc --noEmit is clean after next typegen. The first attempt ran out of memory; it passes with NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144. eslint is clean on the changed files.

Library build run with npm run build for the 3 ids. validate-workflows --shared against the CPU ComfyUI (0.41.0) answers missing_node_type for every graph, because the packs are not installed there, so all three stay validated:false. The graphs are checked against the hand-recorded node definitions. Nothing was run end to end.

Browser check: new tests/e2e/kandinsky6.mjs in demo mode on pnpm dev -p 3471, at 1440 and 390 px, light and dark, on both engines, covering the Video studio, Upscale → Video and Lipsync. 98 checks passed, with no page errors, no console errors and no sideways scroll. The first run caught a hydration mismatch on the Lipsync link, now fixed. Server stopped and .next deleted afterwards (.next/types regenerated for tsc).
left: Nothing has run on a GPU, and fal was never called (no key here). The graphs need a GPU ComfyUI 0.38 or newer with both packs installed (install-comfyui.sh does this) before they can be validated. They should then be checked for: VAEDecode of the joint latent, GetVideoComponents audio on a silent clip going into the VSR, the beautifier loading qwen3.5_9b_bf16 with CLIPLoader type qwen_image as the template does, and Fuobe's 16:9 480p size of 848x480 (the template uses 864x480).

VRAM figures are estimates because none are published. Lite is set at 24 GB in the manifest. Pro distill holds a 60.3 GB DiT, so it needs about an 80 GB GPU or heavy offload. Pre-flight uses the graph's single vramGb of 24, so it doesn't warn when Pro is picked.

The audio VAE file the pack loads, v1-44.pth, is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial), so Models & licences flags the open Kandinsky graphs. Kandinsky's own MIT audio_vae safetensors, shipped in its Diffusers repos, might work with the pack's loader (which accepts .safetensors), but this is unverified. Owner decision: keep the file as it is, or test the MIT one on a GPU.
The audio_vae folder is registered by the pack under the name kandinsky6_audio_vae, so the pre-flight's folder listing may not see v1-44.pth or bigvgan_vocoder/* until the pack is loaded.
Core ComfyUI PR #16825 (native Kandinsky 6) is not in 0.41 or 0.42. If it merges, move the graphs to core nodes.
fal's VSR Lite page quotes $0.08 for 480p→1080p at the same $0.00036 per-MP-per-frame rate. Only the full 5-step VSR endpoint is routed; VSR Lite is recorded in research but not routed.
Not done: the upscale_factor option on the fal generation endpoints (generate and upscale in one call) and the non-distilled Pro and Lite checkpoints (50 steps, CFG 5, MagCache).

Brief corrections: Lite's step range is 4-16, so the brief's Fast 8 / Standard 20 / Best 50 applies to Pro only; Lite uses 4/10/16. Pro i2v costs $0.25/$0.58/$1.40. The brief's '$1.53 to 1080p' is Pro t2v at 50 steps plus $0.18. The ComfyUI templates default to Pro distilled, but Fuobe's open engine defaults to Lite so it runs on ordinary GPUs.
impl.docsNotes: For STATUS/FEATURES on the docs pass: Kandinsky 6.0 (Kandinsky Lab, MIT) is in the Video studio on both engines. It makes 5 s clips at 480p and 24 fps with sound and lip-synced dialogue, from words or a first frame. On the open engine Lite is the default, Pro is optional, and there is a Prompt helper; in the cloud, fal's Pro or Lite at Fast, Standard or Best steps are priced per clip. Kandinsky VSR is in Upscale → Video on both engines at 2x, 2.25x or 4x, for clips up to 5 s, priced at $0.00036 per output MP per frame in the cloud. Lipsync & avatars links to it for a 'talking character from words'. Prompt tip: put spoken words in quotes and end with 'Sound: …'. SELF-HOSTING: install-comfyui.sh now installs the kandinsky6 and kandinsky6-sr packs (K6_PACKS=0 skips them). The file downloads are Lite 6.4 GB, Qwen2.5-VL 7B bf16 16.6 GB, the audio VAE 1.2 GB plus BigVGAN, optionally Pro 60 GB, optionally the Qwen3.5 9B helper 19.3 GB, and the VSR bundle about 17.5 GB. Licence note: the audio VAE v1-44.pth is CC BY-NC 4.0, and the HunyuanVideo VAE's licence excludes the EU, UK and South Korea. Research corrections are in the 'left' field; new-models-10.json now holds the Kandinsky endpoint records.

findings.summary: The pre-flight can never see the BigVGAN vocoder, so open Kandinsky 6.0 always reads Needs setup and an account's run on its own ComfyUI is refused.
findings.detail: The audio files sit in folder 'audio_vae'. ComfyUI has no model folder of that name: the kandinsky6 pack registers models/audio_vae as 'kandinsky6_audio_vae' (nodes.py:31), and the live CPU ComfyUI's /models has no audio_vae (GET /models/audio_vae answers 404). gather.ts therefore records audio_vae as folderMissing. v1-44.pth is still found through the Kandinsky6AudioVAELoader.tod_vae list. bigvgan_vocoder/bigvgan_generator.pt has presence 'list' and no loader, so filePresence returns 'missing' even when it is installed. I checked this with a probe on requirements.json and an inventory of a ComfyUI with the pack loaded: v1-44.pth present, bigvgan_generator.pt missing. As a result the 'Video with dialogue' row and the oss-kandinsky6 chip never read Ready. gateGeneration (preflight is on by default) returns ok:false for an account's ComfyUI, so accounts can't run either Kandinsky graph, and the fix plan keeps asking them to download BigVGAN again. tests/kandinsky6.test.ts never checks readiness against an inventory, so this went unnoticed.
findings.fix: List the folder under the name ComfyUI reports (kandinsky6_audio_vae, still downloading to models/audio_vae), or mark the bigvgan files unobservable like the config.json. Add a readiness test with an inventory of a ComfyUI that has the packs loaded.

findings.summary: The 19.3 GB Qwen3.5 9B prompt-helper file is required even though the Prompt helper is off by default and its nodes are removed from the run.
findings.detail: requirements.json lists text_encoders/qwen3.5_9b_bf16.safetensors under files, not optional, for both graphs. PROMPT_HELPER_OPT_IN drops nodes 19 and 20 unless promptHelper is 'on' (a probe of prepareWorkflow shows no node 20 by default). The pre-flight still asks for a 19 GB download nobody uses by default, and the gate blocks an account that lacks it. The reverse gap exists too: the Pro transformer (60 GB) is optional, and the gate adds an optional file only for Qwen-Image 2.1's clean VAE. So Quality 'pro' without the file is never caught before the run, and vramGb 24 never warns for Pro's roughly 80 GB.
findings.fix: Move qwen3.5_9b_bf16 to optionalModels. In gateGeneration, add it when extra.promptHelper is 'on' and the Pro file when quality is 'pro', the way CLEAN_VAE is handled.

findings.summary: Kandinsky VSR accepts a resolution outside its 2x / 2.25x / 4x tiers, and the two engines then do different things.
findings.detail: planGeneration doesn't check params.resolution against options.resolutions. Probe with params.resolution '1080p' (an API call, a chain or a Reuse from another upscaler) on a 1280x720 clip: the cloud payload is {video_url, upscale_factor: 1.5}, but fal's enum takes only 2, 2.25 or 4, so the run fails at fal. estimateCost prices it at the 2x fallback. The open engine quietly runs 2.25x (factorTier('1080p') is undefined, so the default applies).
findings.fix: Refuse any resolution that isn't one of the model's factor tiers before the run, with a plain message, on both engines. Or map it to the nearest tier the same way on both engines.

findings.summary: fal's Kandinsky VSR needs width and height in multiples of 16 for 2x and 4x, and nothing checks this before the run.
findings.detail: The research record for fal-ai/kandinsky6-vsr says: 'For 2x and 4x upscaling, width and height must be multiples of 16.' An 854x480 clip at 2x is sent anyway and fails at fal. The open pack pads the source itself (source_padding), so this affects the cloud engine only.
findings.fix: Have clipBlocker and the server's upscale check refuse such a clip in the cloud, or suggest 2.25x, with a plain message.

findings.summary: The cloud Lite routes take no negative prompt, but kandinsky-6 still shows the field, and what is typed is dropped without a word.
findings.detail: options.negativePrompt is true for the whole model. A probe shows the lite-best payload without negative_prompt while pro-fast carries it. The UI doesn't say that Lite ignores it.
findings.fix: Hide the negative prompt or add a note when Quality is Lite (for example engineOptions-style per-variant options), or state it in the Quality labels.

findings.file: src/server/request-schema.ts:100, src/server/generations.ts (input built from ...plan.params, then Object.assign(input, source))
findings.summary: A size the client states (params.sourceSize) now reaches GenInput.sourceSize for every model when the server can't read the clip's header.
findings.detail: The schema used to strip sourceSize. Now it is copied into input through ...plan.params, and `source` replaces it only when mediaFacts finds a width and height. Factor upscalers such as Topaz and FLUX Upscale then compute upscale_factor from the client's claim, and the VSR's price follows it. The browser sends true values, so only API callers are affected.
findings.fix: Price with params.sourceSize before the run, but delete it from input before the header is merged, so only the server's own header read sets GenInput.sourceSize.

findings.summary: Every quoted phrase becomes a spoken line, and a prompt made only of a 'Sound:' line gets no sound tags.
findings.detail: Probe: 'A sign reads "OPEN" in neon' becomes 'A sign reads <S>OPEN<E> in neon', so the character speaks the sign. 'Sound: rain' on its own is left untagged because m.index is 0. The placeholder does explain the quotes rule, so this is a known trade-off.
findings.fix: Take quotes as speech only after a speech verb or a colon, or accept the trade-off and say it in the tip. Tag a prompt that is only a sound line.

review.verdict: changes-requested: one high finding (the pre-flight never sees the BigVGAN vocoder in 'audio_vae', so the open Kandinsky graphs stay Needs setup and accounts' runs on their own ComfyUI are refused) and two medium findings (the 19 GB helper file is required while the helper is off and Pro's file and VRAM are never checked; VSR accepts a non-factor resolution and the engines then diverge, with the cloud sending a factor fal rejects). The rest of the package, including the cloud routing, payloads, prices, graphs, licences and the Lipsync link, checks out against the packs' source and fal's pages.

fix.finalSummary: Open engine (your ComfyUI): Kandinsky 6.0 text or image to video with sound (Lite by default, Pro optional, Prompt helper optional), and Kandinsky VSR at 2x, 2.25x or 4x for clips up to 5 s. Built and checked against the packs' source and the node definitions recorded by hand; nothing has run on a GPU. The GPU pre-flight now sees the vocoder where the pack lists it, so a ComfyUI that has everything reads Ready. The 19 GB helper and the 60 GB Pro file are asked for only when the run picks them, both on the board and in the check before a run, so an account's run on its own ComfyUI is no longer refused for files it doesn't use. Cloud engine (fal, needs the owner's key; never called here): kandinsky-6 Pro or Lite at fal's step prices, and kandinsky-vsr priced per output megapixel per frame. Payloads and prices are tested. A non-tier factor is refused on both engines before the run, a clip whose sides fal can't take at 2x or 4x is refused with a pointer to 2.25x, and Lite's labels say it takes no negative prompt. The upscale factor is now made only from the clip's own header, for every factor upscaler. Public sign-up: guests browse the studios read-only. Accounts run the open Kandinsky graphs only on their own ComfyUI, with the pre-flight above, and the cloud stays the owner's. No new routes, and inputs go through the existing account checks.
left: Nothing has run on a GPU or with a fal key. On a GPU ComfyUI with both packs: validate the 3 graphs, check the joint-latent decode and the VSR on a silent clip, the beautifier's loader, and 848x480.

The pack's tod_vae list falls back to 'v1-44.pth' when its folder is empty, so the loader check can report v1-44.pth present when it isn't. The run itself would then fail. Reading it through the kandinsky6_audio_vae listing first would need filePresence to prefer the listing for this file.
VRAM: the pre-flight uses vramGb 24 for both variants. Pro (a 60 GB DiT) needs about 80 GB and doesn't warn.
